statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). NQ trades at 29,457.25, up 0.03%, mid-band inside a 68-point Globex range from 29,426.75 to 29,495.25. A marginal new high at 29,495.25 was made and immediately given back, and Tokyo has converted a lower open into a 64,000.23 session high, recovering 892 points from its low. Both are direct mean-reversion evidence, so Tail eases to 14. Stress stays high at 66: WTI is extending at 102.70, the 10-year holds 4.961% after Monday's 5.012% breach was rejected, and a two-day Federal Reserve meeting opens today with a rate increase priced at roughly 90%.
recommendation: Tail at 14 sits in the low band, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Six independent mean-reversion events are now on the record across this window: Monday's cash index recovered 417 points off its low, the 10-year's move above 5% was erased, crude gave back part of an intraday spike, Tokyo's lower open became a session high, that high extended again to 64,000.23, and NQ's own marginal Globex high was rejected within the hour. Stress remains high at 66 because the energy and long-yield backdrop is unresolved, but Stress alone does not change the mapped state. The narrow danger window spanning 13:00 to 15:00 UTC covers the US cash open and the first full cash hour, where the conditional path peaks at 23, still below the block threshold.
headline: NQ holds a 68-point Globex band at 29,457 and rejects a marginal new high while Tokyo extends to 64,000; crude runs to $102.70 and the 10-year holds 4.961% as a two-day Fed meeting opens priced for a hike - Tail eases to 14 with Stress high at 66
body:
The current hour rests on live evidence rather than an evidence gap, and the evidence strengthens the mean-reversion reading. CME equity index futures have traded since the 22:00 UTC reopen inside a band 68 points wide, from 29,426.75 to 29,495.25, and NQ is currently 29,457.25, up 0.03% against a 29,449.50 previous close. The important detail is where in that band price sits. NQ printed a marginal new session high at 29,495.25, a little above the 29,492.75 extreme that stood an hour ago, and then retraced roughly forty points back to the middle of the range within the same hour. A failed extension of that kind is the single most direct piece of evidence against the pathological no-retracement path that Tail measures, and it is the reason Tail eases by a point rather than holding.

Tokyo has continued to run in the opposite direction without pulling NQ with it. The Nikkei 225 opened at 63,190.37, below its 63,492.99 previous close, traded down to 63,067.18, and now stands at 63,959.56, up 0.73%, after printing a 64,000.23 session high. That is a recovery of roughly 892 points from the low and a second extension beyond the level reported an hour ago. Japanese strength of that size has not transmitted into NQ, which has instead eased from the top of its band. The divergence keeps the dominant mode at mixed and argues against treating either market's move as the start of a shared one-way regime.

Monday resolved as a two-sided, rotational session rather than a broad liquidation. The Nasdaq-100 cash index gapped 1.63% below its 29,368.44 previous close, bottomed at 28,867.67, rallied 417 points to 29,285.50 and closed at 29,127.16, down 0.82%. The S&P 500 fell 0.48% to 7,619.94 and the Dow 0.29% to 52,421.17. The damage was concentrated in semiconductors after public warnings from leading AI developers about the pace of model development: the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 5.9%, with Arm down about 9.7%, Intel about 5.6%, Micron about 5.3% and Broadcom about 4.8%. Against that, communication services rose 2.68%, software indices gained between 2.8% and 3.8%, and Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft all closed higher, leaving the megacap group split four to four. Conflicting breadth of that kind reduces directional conviction and raises Stress; it does not establish the persistent directional efficiency that Tail measures.

The rates and energy backdrop is why Stress sits in the high band and edges up a point. WTI is 102.70, up 1.29% and pressing the top of its 101.83 to 102.98 overnight range, with Brent near 106.96. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which carries roughly 4 to 5 million barrels a day and is the principal bypass of a Strait of Hormuz that has been effectively closed since March, remains shut after the 11 September drone strikes launched from Iraq, with no disclosed repair timeline. The long end is under pressure globally rather than only in the United States: the 10-year yield reached 5.012% on Monday before being rejected and settling at 4.961%, the German 10-year is above 3.51% and at its highest since 2009, and the Japanese 10-year has returned to 3.00% ahead of a Bank of Japan meeting that is widely expected to deliver a 25 basis point increase to 1.25% on Friday. The VIX closed at 17.10, up 7.95%, elevated but well short of disorderly.

The scheduled path through this window is well defined and the largest catalyst falls outside it. The Federal Open Market Committee begins a two-day meeting today, but the decision at 18:00 UTC on 16 September and the press conference at 18:30 UTC both fall beyond this 24-hour window, as does Retail Sales at 12:30 UTC that day. Within the window, weekly ADP employment lands near 12:15 UTC, the Empire State manufacturing index near 12:30 UTC, a 20-year bond auction near 17:00 UTC against a 5.204% prior yield, and the API crude stock estimate near 20:30 UTC. The auction is the clearest scheduled mechanism for restarting the long-yield leg and is the reason the conditional path lifts again late in the U.S. afternoon. Shared delayed cross-asset context collected at 01:00 UTC returned a partial status, with its calendar section unavailable but its futures, breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections complete. Its futures readings of NQ and ES marginally higher, crude firmer, gold softer and Treasury futures modestly lower align with the independently verified picture above, and it is used as confirmation only, never as live price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments are available. Tail entered the window at 19, held a 19 to 21 plateau through the Asian session, rose to a 26 peak during the European morning chip-led decline and repeated 25 in the following hour, eased through midday, printed 26 again at the US cash open, then decayed steadily through the afternoon and evening to a 15 to 16 plateau across the last four hours as the opening gap was recovered. Stress fell from a 79 peak to 65 and Confidence held between 85 and 89. The window contains three hours in the orange band, all tied to the chip-led decline, and no hour reached the red band.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds the low band through the remainder of the Asian session, easing to an overnight floor of 14 before drifting to 15 and 16 into the Tokyo close. It rises to 17 for the European opening auction and 19 at the European cash open, enters the watch band at 21 across the two European mid-morning hours that produced Monday's chip-led leg, eases to 20 through the midday lull, returns to 21 for the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC releases, and peaks at 23 across the 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. It eases to 21 and 20 through the US midday, lifts to 22 for the 20-year bond auction near 17:00 UTC, holds 21 through the post-auction hour and the final cash hour before Federal Reserve decision day, then falls to 19 at the cash close, 17 after it, and 16 during the CME maintenance halt. It closes the window at 17 for the Globex reopen and 18 across the Tokyo cash open on decision day. No hour in the window reaches the block threshold on current evidence. Stress stays in the high band throughout, peaking at 73 across the danger window, and Confidence decays from 88 to 67 as the live evidence behind this assessment ages.
